note: The emulators BrokenDev tests the homebrew games on, besides BrokenNes (the reference column of every result). A package is one official release zip, pinned by URL, size and sha256, unpacked portable into BROKENDEV_HOME\emulators\<package>-<version>. One package can back several emulator ids (BizHawk: NesHawk for the NES, BSNES for the SNES). Validated by lib\Emulators.ps1 (Test-BdEmulators) and tests\run-tests.ps1. Download hosts are also checked against a fixed list in lib\Emulators.ps1: editing this file alone cannot add a new download source.

packages.title: Mesen 2
packages.sha256Source: GitHub's published digest of the release asset
packages.portable: Mesen is portable when a settings.json sits beside Mesen.exe; otherwise it uses Documents\Mesen2 (which Super VRUN's own tests use on this machine). BrokenDev writes that settings.json before every start (lib\Emulators.ps1, Set-BdMesenSettings), so its Mesen never reads or writes Documents\Mesen2.
packages.prerequisites: .NET 8 desktop runtime is bundled (single-file exe); no system component needed.

packages.title: BizHawk (EmuHawk)
packages.sha256Source: GitHub's published digest of the release asset
packages.portable: BizHawk keeps everything beside EmuHawk.exe unless --config names another config.ini. BrokenDev always passes --config=<scratch>\config.ini, whose path settings point every save, state and screenshot folder into the run's scratch folder.
packages.prerequisites: .NET Framework 4.8 and the Visual C++ 2015-2022 x64 runtime (checked by 'emulators': both present on this machine on 2026-10-22).

packages.title: FCEUX
packages.sha256Source: GitHub's published digest of the release asset
packages.portable: The Windows build keeps fceux.cfg beside fceux64.exe and makes its folders there; '-cfg' takes a file NAME joined to the exe's folder ('A pathname can NOT be specified', 2.7.0 help), and FCEUX writes the config back on exit. So BrokenDev never runs the installed copy: every run gets a copy of fceux64.exe and its DLLs (7.6 MB) in its scratch folder with a fresh fceux.cfg (battery saves -> the run's save folder, every other folder in the scratch folder). The adapter checks that the installed folder did not change.

packages.title: Snes9x
packages.sha256Source: measured by BrokenDev on 2026-10-22 (GitHub publishes no digest for this asset)
packages.portable: The Windows build reads snes9x.conf beside its exe; '-conf <file>' names another one. BrokenDev passes -conf <scratch>\snes9x.conf with its save, snapshot and movie folders in the run's scratch folder.

emulators.title: BrokenNes (Workshop, headless)

defaults.ramInit: NES: the FCEUX pattern 00 00 00 00 FF FF FF FF (the app default; a project may ask powerOnRam zeros). SNES: zeros.
defaults.overscan: none: the NES picture is 256x240, the SNES 256x224 (or 239)
defaults.cores: the app defaults: NES CPU/PPU/APU FIX, SNES SFC; a project's verify.cores wins

emulators.notes: The same Workshop and cores as 'verify'; deterministic, so a reference result can be compared run to run.

emulators.title: Mesen 2.1.1

defaults.ramInit: Mesen's own default (recorded per run in compat.json from the settings it ran with)

emulators.notes: Driven with Lua through --testRunner (the API the 20 VRUN tracers use). Input is set on the inputPolled event. Audio activity is not measured (the Lua API has no audio access).

emulators.title: BizHawk 2.11.1, NesHawk core

defaults.overscan: NesHawk clips 8 lines top and bottom by default: pictures are 256x224

emulators.notes: EmuHawk --lua=<script> --config=<scratch config.ini> (NES -> NesHawk pinned, sound off, unthrottled). Input with joypad.set, frames with emu.frameadvance, memory.read_u8 on the core's RAM domain, client.screenshot.

emulators.title: FCEUX 2.7.0

defaults.region: NTSC (palyo 0, dendy 0; also for a NES 2.0 'multiple region' header)
defaults.ramInit: 00 00 00 00 FF FF FF FF repeated (RAMInitOption 0, measured before the first frame)
defaults.overscan: the window shows lines 8-231 (srendline 8, erendline 231); BrokenDev's pictures have all 240 lines
defaults.other: old PPU (newppu 0), 8 sprites a line, FCEUX's built-in palette

emulators.notes: fceux64.exe -lua <script> <rom> on a private copy. Input with joypad.set(1, ...) every frame (held during frame f+1 when set at framecount f), memory.readbyte, the picture with gui.gdscreenshot(true) (the frame just completed, 256x240; gui.savescreenshotas saves the NEXT frame cropped to 224 lines, so it is not used), sound activity from sound.get() (channel volumes, sound output off), emu.speedmode('nothrottle') (every frame rendered), a clean exit with emu.exit (the battery save is written on close). Two windows (FCEUX and its Lua console) show during a run; they cannot be hidden. Mapper-30 saves: the .sav is the WHOLE 512 KB PRG flash, written on every close and run from at the next power-on, so a save folder must be emptied when the ROM changes (BrokenDev does).

emulators.title: Snes9x 1.63 (standalone)

defaults.overscan: 256x224 (239 when the game turns overscan on)

emulators.notes: No scripting in the standalone build. Input comes from a .smv movie BrokenDev writes; pictures from its own frame dump. It cannot read game memory: its column checks pictures only and says so.

emulators.title: BizHawk 2.11.1, BSNES core
emulators.notes: As bizhawk-neshawk with SNES -> BSNES pinned; work RAM through the WRAM domain.
